claim: The note calls まちます the plain/dictionary form, but the deck already taught me (chapter-0 note) that the base verb is まつ, and every verb I know ends in ます.
evidence: Back note: 'Plain/dictionary form of まってください (please wait) — て-form (まって) + ください makes the polite request.' Compare chapter-0/chotto-matte-kudasai note: 'まって is the て-form of まつ (matsu, "to wait") plus ください'.
fix: Reword the note to say まちます is the ます form of the verb behind まってください (whose dictionary form is まつ), not its dictionary form.
verdictReason: Rendered back reads "Plain/dictionary form of まってください". まちます is the polite ます form; the dictionary form is まつ, which the deck itself names in the chapter-0 chotto-matte-kudasai note and cards in chapter-15 (matsu-dict-form, "Wait (dictionary form)"). The book glosses it simply "まちます wait". A false grammar label on the back is a blocker. Preflight only flags this note for missing romaji, not the label.

verdictReason: Rendered back reads "see that card for the plain dictionary form", pointing at machimasu: the same false label, so fix both together. The て-form description itself is correct.

evidence: Back note: 'いい (ii) is the one irregular い-adjective: its negative is よくないです (yokunai desu), never いくない'. Same unit: cool | かっこいい | 'Cool / stylish, good-looking', no note on its negative.

What is real is that the same extras unit cards かっこいい (cool) with nothing on its negative, and the book never teaches かっこいい at all. If acted on, the line belongs on the cool card's note (かっこいい negates as かっこよくない because it contains いい), not on this one. Owner's call; polish.

fix: Add a note to ookii-uchi-ne (or a new おおきい こうえん card) saying an い-adjective goes straight before the noun with no な, unlike きれいな はな.

evidence: Book, NOTES 3: "はい、いただきます。 This phrase is spoken when taking something that is offered. It implies both acceptance and gratitude." Dialogue English: "Yes, please." Card: target いただきます, English "Yes, thank you. (I'll gladly accept.)"

The "Yes," renders the book's はい from the dialogue and NOTES 3 (はい、いただきます), which the target drops, so on Production the English prompts はい、いただきます and the answer is いただきます. Either fix works; changing the target also removes the target collision with chapter-0/itadakimasu (currently held apart by the scene) but changes the audio, so dropping "Yes," from the English is the smaller edit.
